newsitem.title: HONG KONG: EDS and HK's Cargonet in strategic alliance.
newsitem.headline: EDS and HK's Cargonet in strategic alliance.

text.p: CargoNet, the Hong Kong-based electronic service provider to the air and sea cargo industry, has signed a strategic alliance pact with the U.S.-based Electronic Data Systems Corp, CargoNet's chief executive officer, Ian Craig, told Reuters.
The service, technology and marketing agreement signed in Hong Kong is aimed at developing electronic commerce services in Hong Kong and southern China.
Craig forecast major growth this year with a five to six times growth in revenue and a target of "several million U.S. dollars".

"This puts us in a strong position. We get to exploit their technology and they get to exploit our local expertise. It's a pretty good marriage in that sense and a major endorsement for us as the cargo community system for Hong Kong. The whole field of electronic commerce is evolving rapidly and EDS' commitment and support will help maintain a decisive technological lead," Craig said in an interview.
CargoNet specialises in real-time logistics and "track and trace" systems.

CargoNet is backed by a shareholder group comprising: EDS; HIT Holdings Ltd; Kenwa Communication Co Ltd; Traxon Asia (a joint venture between Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Japan Airlines Ltd and Korean Airlines ; the Hongkong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents; and the local CSSL Group.

As part of the agreement, EDS has purchased for an undisclosed sum a stake in Transportation Community Network Ltd, which operates CargoNet, gained a seat on the board and becomes an equal partner with major shareholders HIT, the CSSL Group, and Kenwa Communication.
Craig declined to detail the equity arrangements but said new shares have been issued. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
